status: design brief; not an implemented autonomous service
purpose: Interview a brand owner, apply a central theme to a distributable copy of the DesignA11y system and Figma file, and retain accessibility contracts.

context: audiences, access needs and contexts of use
voice, content domains, languages and tone
existing identity assets, rights and non-negotiable choices
aesthetic: visual personality and reference examples with specific likes/dislikes
palette anchors, semantic roles and light/dark needs
type families, licensing, hierarchy, weights, density and reading metrics
corner radius scale and intentional fixed geometry
border widths, line style and icon language
gradient stops, angle, intensity and reading-zone constraints
shadow, elevation, depth and surface treatment
interaction character, timing and preference alternatives
imagery: photography versus illustration, abstract surfaces or mixed media
image style references, desired meaning and excluded tropes
background references and relationship to brand mission
texture, finish, feature scale, density and sensory intensity
whether tactile/sensory surfaces fit this brand at all
quiet reading zones, contrast, crop and responsive behavior
representational inclusion, alt purpose, copyright and consent

workflow: Retrieve current public Specs, contracts and token/style inventory.
Interview in short stages, distinguishing required questions from safe defaults.
Produce a reviewable brand profile and theme mapping with explicit accessibility conflicts.
Create a separate copy; preserve the original DesignA11y reference.
Apply primitives/semantic aliases/shared styles centrally; preserve master-instance relationships.
Update copy-specific Specs, examples and agent guidance to the new brand context.
Validate inheritance with a second-theme change and audit unsupported fields and literals.
Run relevant full AI A11y Toolkit references, visual and manual/AT checks; document unresolved findings.
Deliver Figma copy, theme profile, token export, mappings, validation evidence.
inheritedRequirements: text and non-text contrast targets, revalidated after theming
sensory role assessment without universal comfort or health claims
acceptance: Brand questionnaire covers all style domains and context.
Theme changes propagate without individual component edits.
New brand has its own POV; DesignA11y sensory aesthetics are optional rather than universal.
Accessibility requirements remain; actual resulting experience is revalidated.
Provenance is transparent, documented and does not phone home.
